title: Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula Rishikesh | History, Things to Do & Travel Guide
content:
About Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula - Rishikesh,

Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula are the two most iconic suspension bridges in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, built across the sacred Ganga River. These iron bridges not only connect the banks of the river but also symbolize the city’s spiritual charm and cultural heritage.

  • Laxman Jhula (450 ft long): Built in 1930, it is believed that Laxman (younger brother of Lord Ram) crossed the river here on a jute rope. Today, it stands as a popular tourist attraction with temples, yoga centers, and cafes around.
  • Ram Jhula (750 ft long): Constructed in 1986, this bridge connects Sivananda Ashram with Swarg Ashram. It is longer and less crowded than Laxman Jhula, offering panoramic views of the Ganga and surrounding hills.

Both bridges are pedestrian-friendly but also allow motorbikes. Walking across them is an unforgettable experience, with the sound of temple bells, chanting of mantras, and the sight of the flowing Ganga creating a magical atmosphere.

Surrounded by ashrams, temples, shops, and eateries, Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula are must-visit landmarks that reflect the true soul of Rishikesh.

Best Time to Visit Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula Rishikesh:

  • Peak Season (October - March): Pleasant weather with average temperatures 10°C - 25°C. Best time for sightseeing, photography, and exploring cafes & ashrams.
  • Moderate Season (April - June): Warm and sunny, with temperatures 20°C - 35°C. Perfect for spiritual walks and short visits, though afternoons can be hot.
  • Low Season (July - September): Monsoon season with average temperatures 18°C - 30°C. Bridges are open, but expect occasional rain and slippery paths. Scenic beauty is at its peak.

Things to Do at/Near Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula:

  • Walk across the iconic suspension bridges.
  • Visit Trayambakeshwar Temple near Laxman Jhula.
  • Explore Sivananda Ashram and Parmarth Niketan Ashram.
  • Enjoy riverbank cafes with Ganga views.
  • Shop for spiritual books, handicrafts, and souvenirs.
  • Capture sunset photography over the Ganga.

How to Reach Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula:

  • By Road: Easily reachable by taxi, auto, or rickshaw within Rishikesh.
  • By Train: Rishikesh railway station (5 km away).
  • By Air: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (22 km).

Best Places to Visit Near Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula (within 50 km):

1- Triveni Ghat (2 km): Famous for evening Ganga Aarti.

2- Parmarth Niketan Ashram (1 km): Spiritual retreat and yoga hub.

3- Beatles Ashram (3 km): Known for meditation and wall art.

4- Neelkanth Mahadev Temple (32 km): A holy Shiva temple in the forest.

5- Rajaji National Park (18 km - Chilla Gate): Perfect for wildlife safaris.

6- Kunjapuri Temple (25 km): Scenic temple with sunrise views.

7- Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar (28 km): Sacred ghat for Ganga Aarti.

8- Mansa Devi Temple, Haridwar (30 km): Popular Shakti Peeth with ropeway access.

9- Chandi Devi Temple, Haridwar (32 km): Hilltop temple with panoramic views.

10- Daksha Mahadev Temple, Kankhal (33 km): Mythological Shiva temple near Haridwar.
excerpt: Ram Jhula & Laxman Jhula Rishikesh are iconic suspension bridges across the Ganga, blending mythology, spirituality, and scenic beauty. Surrounded by ashrams, temples, and cafes, they are must-visit landmarks offering a unique mix of devotion, culture, and adventure.

faqs.question: Why is Laxman Jhula famous?
faqs.answer: It is believed that Laxman crossed the Ganga here on a rope, making it mythologically significant.

faqs.question: How far are Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula from each other?
faqs.answer: About 2 km apart, both walkable or reachable by auto.

faqs.question: What is the length of Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula?
faqs.answer: Ram Jhula – 750 ft, Laxman Jhula – 450 ft.

faqs.question: Can vehicles cross the bridges?
faqs.answer: Yes, two-wheelers are allowed, but four-wheelers are not.

faqs.question: What are the timings of Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula?
faqs.answer: Open 24/7, though evenings are most lively.
